correctness.summary: Necessity follows from the sharp obstruction sK_3 disjoint union K_m. For sufficiency, Birken's theorem handles vectors with all class sizes at most s. If a size-(s+1) class occurs, every maximum-degree-two graph has an independent feedback set of exactly s+1 vertices; removing it leaves a linear forest, where the remaining target multiplicities satisfy the sharp no-equal-adjacencies bound. Exhaustive definition-level verification through order 12 found no discrepancy.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Birken's arXiv:2609.18629v1 states the remainder-sensitive condition as Conjecture 5 and identifies the extremal graph, but the inspected text does not prove the maximum-degree-two case. Searches across prescribed/fixed/given class-size terminology, maximum degree two, paths, cycles, and skewed coloring found no earlier exact universal characterization. No concrete inaccessible source was identified as likely to contain the same theorem; residual risk comes from older literature using different terminology for colorings with prescribed multiplicities.

value.summary: The result settles the first nontrivial maximum-degree case of a newly stated Hajnal-Szemeredi-type conjecture and strengthens it to an exact universal feasibility characterization. The proof exposes a simple structural mechanism via independent feedback sets and linear forests.

limitations: The theorem does not address maximum degree at least three.
The smaller-class range invokes Birken's Theorem 1.
Terminological variation in older coloring literature leaves residual originality risk.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
